findings.title: Three rulebook hats call rulebook-section access a `substrate`, which the catalogue defines as something else
locations: catalog/hats/doc-policy.toml:6: "the rulebook sections named in your substrate — {package.rulebook_sections}"
catalog/hats/naming-policy.toml:6: "the rulebook sections named in your substrate FIRST"
catalog/hats/invariants-and-decisions.toml:6: "the rulebook sections named in your substrate FIRST"
catalog/hats/README.md:3: "substrate (`full` — the whole rendered site incl. the design docs; `siteonly` — ...)"
src/CLI/Preflight.jl:254: "What ELSE a hat is handed is `needs`, never a substrate value"
findings.description: `substrate` is a closed two-value field (`full`/`siteonly`) naming which corpus view a hat gets; rulebook-section access is a `needs` grant, and Preflight.jl's own resolve_hats docstring is explicit that this is 'never a substrate value.' Yet doc-policy, naming-policy and invariants-and-decisions all instruct their agent to read 'the rulebook sections named in your substrate' — attributing a `needs`-granted resource to the wrong catalogue field. A reader of just these three persona strings (the cold-read test the docs-rubric itself applies) would reasonably conclude `substrate` carries rulebook content, which schema/hat.schema.json and the README both contradict.
findings.resolution_hint: Reword the three personas to 'the rulebook sections you are handed' or 'named in {package.rulebook_sections}' rather than 'named in your substrate', so the term `substrate` stays reserved for its one closed-vocabulary meaning.

findings.title: hats/README.md documents a `{policy.<file>}` placeholder no generic hat ever uses
locations: catalog/hats/README.md:7: "and `{policy.<file>}` are filled by the CLI"
catalog/hats/*.toml: no occurrence of the literal `{policy.` token in any of the 22 files
findings.description: The README's placeholder list for hat personas names `{package.name}`, `{package.description}`, `{package.domain}`, `{package.terms}`, `{package.deliberate_absences}`, `{package.rulebook_sections}` and `{policy.<file>}` as the substitutions the CLI fills. `substitute()` (src/CLI/Preflight.jl:220-227) does implement `{policy.<file>}`, reading `.gbg/policy/<file>.md` — but not one of the 22 catalog/hats/*.toml personas contains that token; the rulebook-reading hats instead reference `{package.rulebook_sections}` or name the policy file in plain prose ("the rendered policy file `docs-rubric.md`"). The claim that this placeholder is part of the hats' own vocabulary is accordingly unverifiable from the catalogue that is supposed to demonstrate it.
findings.resolution_hint: Either drop `{policy.<file>}` from the hats/README.md placeholder list (it may only ever be used by a consumer's own .gbg/hats/*.toml, which is outside this catalogue), or point to the one hat that is meant to demonstrate it.

findings.title: check-docs.toml's `family` lane names itself "CHECK 7", a number the catalogue never defines
locations: catalog/lanes/check-docs.toml:26: "YOUR LANE IS CHECK 7, WHICH NO PER-SURFACE AGENT CAN RUN"
catalog/lanes/check-docs.toml:6-18: the `[surface]` brief enumerates only checks 1 through 6
findings.description: The `[surface]` brief numbers its own checklist 1 (CORRECT) through 6 (CITED). The `family` cross-lane brief calls its own concern "CHECK 7", and the `cold-reader` and `operational-claims` cross-lane briefs refer back to "CHECK 2's audience half" and "CHECK 1's operational half" respectively — both of which resolve against the surface brief's own numbering. "Check 7" has no such anchor anywhere in the catalogue: nothing in catalog/ enumerates a 7th check, so the label is meaningful only to someone who already knows the reasoning behind the number, which fails the self-containedness bar (RULE.DOC.TERMS_DEFINED / the cold-read test) the catalogue's own check #2 applies to everything else it reviews.
findings.resolution_hint: Either add a seventh bullet to the `[surface]` brief's numbered list (e.g. "7. VARIANT PAIRS") so "CHECK 7" resolves within the catalogue, or drop the numeral and describe the family lane's concern in words alone.
